content: 1. Breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP) inhibitors may increase the systemic exposure of talazoparib, a BCRP substrate. If coadministration cannot be avoided, monitor for potential adverse reactions. 2. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Tecovirimat increases the levels or effects of voxilaprevir and velpatasvir by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Tecovirimat is a weak inhibitor of CYP2C8 and CYP2C19. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if coadministered. 5. Tepotinib increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If concomitant use is unavoidable, reduce the P-gp substrate dosage as recommended in its approved product labeling. 6. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Trofinetide increases the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by inhibiting OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 transporters. Avoid coadministration with sensitive substrates. 8. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of voxilaprevir and velpatasvir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Tucatinib also affects hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the levels or effects of these drugs. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose according to product labeling. 9. Vadadustat increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir by affecting BCRP substrates. Monitor for signs of adverse effects and reduce the substrate dose in accordance with product labeling. 10. Voclosporin increases the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by inhibiting OATP1B1 transporters. Monitor for adverse reactions of OATP1B1 substrates when coadministered with voclosporin. 11. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Voxilaprevir increases the levels or effects of intranasal zavegepant by affecting OATP1B3 transporters. Avoid or use an alternative drug. OATP1B3 inhibitors may significantly increase systemic exposure to zavegepant. 13. Common adverse effects include headache (21-23%), fatigue (17-19%), diarrhea (13-14%), nausea (10-13%), asthenia (4-6%), and insomnia (3-6%). Serious cardiac disorders, such as symptomatic bradycardia, have been reported in patients taking amiodarone who initiated treatment with a sofosbuvir-containing regimen. 14. Skin and subcutaneous tissue reactions, including rashes with blisters or angioedema-like swelling, have been reported. Angioedema may occur. 15. Rifampin significantly decreases serum concentrations of sofosbuvir, velpatasvir, and voxilaprevir. 16. Hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation has been reported. Refer to black box warnings for details. 17. There is no adequate human data to establish whether sofosbuvir/velpatasvir/voxilaprevir poses a risk to pregnancy outcomes. It is unknown if these drugs are distributed in human breast milk. Consider the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding along with the mother’s clinical need for the drug and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed infant. 18. Sofosbuvir inhibits HCV NS5B RNA-dependent polymerase, suppressing viral replication. Velpatasvir is a pangenotypic HCV NS5A inhibitor, essential for viral replication. Voxilaprevir is a pangenotypic NS3/4A protease inhibitor, necessary for proteolytic cleavage of the HCV-encoded polyprotein into mature forms, which is critical for viral replication. 19. Sofosbuvir is metabolized by cathepsin A, CES1, and HINT1. Velpatasvir is metabolized by CYP2B6, CYP2C8, and CYP3A4. Voxilaprevir is metabolized by CYP3A4. 20. Take the medication with food. Store below 30°C (86°F). Dispense only in the original container. 21. The above information is provided for general informational and educational purposes only.
